paper_title: Predicting mortality from AI-based cardiac volumes, mass, an
concern_text: Authors need to use cutoff values from NLST and apply to two independent cohorts, performing same analyses individually. The sole usage of quantiles in each cohort is insufficient — must show actual transferable cut-off values exist.
author_response: Applied NLST-derived cutoffs to independent cohorts showing consistent risk stratification.

paper_title: Predicting mortality from AI-based cardiac volumes, mass, an
concern_text: Statistical analysis needs improvement: p-values not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Stepwise elimination lacks adjustment for known confounders (sex, hypertension, dyslipidemia). Must show model works in stratified analyses for young participants and non-smokers.
author_response: Added multiple comparison correction and consistent confounder adjustment across all cohorts.

paper_title: Predicting mortality from AI-based cardiac volumes, mass, an
concern_text: Bland-Altman plots show >100% variation in smaller volumes (<100mL). How many patients change risk groups between T0 and T1? This has huge clinical impact and could lead to major misclassifications and potentially harm.
author_response: Added reclassification analysis showing proportion changing risk groups and clinical impact assessment.

paper_title: Predicting mortality from AI-based cardiac volumes, mass, an
concern_text: The model should be uploaded to an open-access repository, not only available on reasonable request, as this limits reproducibility.
author_response: Model uploaded to open-access repository.

paper_title: Predicting mortality from AI-based cardiac volumes, mass, an
concern_text: CAC and structural results are so confounded by age, sex, smoking, diabetes that there seems little value in non-risk-adjusted results. ROC for clinical models should be in main figure, not supplementary.
author_response: Moved clinical model ROC to main Figure 6 and de-emphasized unadjusted results.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: Did authors set threshold for missing data to exclude features with high missingness? Were validation models run on complete-case or imputed data? Several features (procalcitonin, D-dimer, troponin) are not routine — how should model be applied when absent?
author_response: Added missing data thresholds, complete-case vs imputed comparison, and model behavior with absent lab values.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: Among 20 features, 'Use of diuretics', 'Admission to ICU', and 'Use of human albumin' vary between centers and have most significant SHAP contribution. This could limit stability and generalizability.
author_response: Added center-specific performance analysis and leave-one-center-out validation.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: Why were patients with AKI in first 24 hours excluded? These seem like the patients you'd want to identify — many Stage 1 AKI within 24h develop Stage 2/3 over next 24-72h. Why exclude baseline creatinine <0.6 mg/dL — these include older patients and cancer patients at high risk.
author_response: Added sensitivity analysis including early AKI and low-baseline patients.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: Imputing normal values for procalcitonin/troponin when not tested is problematic — if 80% of cohort has imputed normal values, this creates systematic bias. Tests not ordered may indicate clinical judgment that the patient is lower risk.
author_response: Added missingness indicator variables and analysis of informative missingness.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: Almost all 95% CIs of AUC values are either very narrow or similar to mean estimate. Models and AUC estimates obtained through multiple iterative testings may increase likelihood of false positive findings.
author_response: Clarified CI calculation method and added bootstrap CIs.

paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model f
concern_text: 5.4% having AKI across total cohort seems low. 40% of AKI in ICU also seems low. How were duplicate patients handled if same patient had AKI during repeat admission?
author_response: Added AKI incidence comparison with literature and clarified duplicate patient handling.

paper_title: Development and validation of self-monitoring auto-updating
concern_text: How to use multiple imputation in a prospective setting for both individual risk prediction and model updating? How to predict mortality for a patient who misses some predictor values? How to include patients with missing predictors in model updating?
author_response: Added detailed description of real-time imputation strategy using last-observation-carried-forward and mean imputation.

paper_title: Development and validation of self-monitoring auto-updating
concern_text: XGBoost coefficients in Figure 5 — how were they derived and why are they all positive? Also, lactate and log-transformed lactate both included is hard to interpret — were original and log-transformed predictors in variable selection simultaneously?
author_response: Clarified XGBoost feature importance (not coefficients). Removed log-transformed duplicate.

paper_title: Development and validation of self-monitoring auto-updating
concern_text: Line 184, please explain how the 'minority class was oversampled to correct for class imbalance'. Multiple technical terms unexplained: one-hot encoded, passive imputation, AUPR, ICI.
author_response: Added explanations of all technical terms and detailed oversampling methodology.

paper_title: Development and validation of self-monitoring auto-updating
concern_text: Slightly uncertain how much small model performance drifts impact on clinical care when models are used as adjunct only. Practicalities and cost of applying and maintaining the dynamic updating system on larger scale not well discussed.
author_response: Added discussion of implementation cost and clinical impact of calibration drift.

paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models —
concern_text: Empirical validation uses logistic regression which is simple and linearly scales. Rationale for distributed file system is undermotivated for 100-variable LR. Need to demonstrate with significantly larger and more complex models.
author_response: Added XGBoost and MLP experiments.

paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models —
concern_text: XGBoost and MLP are still conventional models. Would be more relevant with transformers, CNNs, LSTM. The concept of federated learning is not new, blockchain technology not new — fail to see significant novelty and technical contributions.
author_response: Clarified that clinical contribution (privacy-preserving multi-site prediction) is the novelty, not the FL algorithm itself.

paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models —
concern_text: Comparison to centralized LR alone is insufficient. Should benchmark against state-of-the-art tree-based algorithms and deep neural networks using the substantial dataset.
author_response: Added centralized XGBoost and MLP comparisons.

paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models —
concern_text: Evaluation should include F1-score, recall, precision, and sensitivity beyond just AUC. Distribution of outcomes and class balance needs clearer presentation.
author_response: Added full metric panel and class distribution table.

paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models —
concern_text: Characteristics of each dataset including demographics and covariates should be clearly outlined in a table.
author_response: Added comprehensive demographics table per site.

paper_title: Machine learning for risk stratification in the emergency de
concern_text: Model showed adequate predictive accuracy but no effect on clinical decision-making or clinical outcomes. Clinical course changed for only 1 single patient of over 600 in the intervention arm. This is a 'negative example' of how NOT to implement a clinical risk score.
author_response: Reframed paper as an implementation science contribution — valuable negative example showing that even accurate models fail without workflow integration.

paper_title: Machine learning for risk stratification in the emergency de
concern_text: Insufficient detail on implementation: no information about what physicians received about the trial beforehand, how the score was integrated into workflow, what training was provided, how alert fatigue was managed.
author_response: Added detailed implementation strategy section with training protocol, workflow integration, and lessons learned.

paper_title: Machine learning for risk stratification in the emergency de
concern_text: Consider 7-day mortality risk instead of 31-day as avenue for better adoption. Future work should involve more user-friendly integration and risk 'zones' (e.g., infection, respiratory concern) rather than a single number.
author_response: Added 7-day mortality analysis and discussed risk zone framework for future implementation.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: Cohort is predominantly HFpEF with <20% HFrEF — surprising. AHF may differ in prognosis and treatment between HFpEF and HFrEF. Would it be better to focus on a specific type?
author_response: Added subtype-specific analysis and discussed clinical implications of the HFpEF-dominant cohort.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: It would be beneficial to provide the TRIPOD statement and checklist. Why use all-cause mortality not specific cause? What particular length of survival is the target?
author_response: Added TRIPOD checklist. Clarified outcome as all-cause mortality at 6/12/24/30 months.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: Need more details on imputation. Is MAR mechanism justified? How much data was missing and for which parameters? Biomarkers may be 'missing' depending on patient's state — healthier patients have fewer examinations.
author_response: Added missing data analysis with MNAR sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: Average age in external cohort much higher than training cohort. All-cause mortality also much higher. Why should this not impact generalizability?
author_response: Discussed age and mortality differences and showed model calibration remained adequate after recalibration.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: The paper lacks detailed comparisons across the 12 ML methods used. How do individual models compare? What is the rationale for the specific ensemble strategy?
author_response: Added individual model performance comparison table and ensemble ablation analysis.

paper_title: AI hybrid survival assessment for advanced heart failure pat
concern_text: Could authors clarify about the database — are these all hospitalization records or both inpatient and outpatient? Missing values — how much data was missing?
author_response: Clarified data source and added comprehensive missing data summary.

paper_title: A wearable-based aging clock associates with disease and beh
concern_text: PpgAge predicts chronological age well but lacks evaluation in predicting age-related outcomes like mortality, incident diseases, or functional outcomes. Must demonstrate additional predictive ability with these outcomes.
author_response: Added disease association analysis and mortality prediction comparison.

paper_title: A wearable-based aging clock associates with disease and beh
concern_text: Detailed breakdowns of consumer wearable types and software versions needed. Are all participants using the same smartwatch model? No comparison of Apple Watch PPG to ground truth. Data processing lacks details on wear time, data quality, missing data handling.
author_response: Added device-specific analysis, PPG validation against clinical-grade devices, and detailed preprocessing workflow.

paper_title: A wearable-based aging clock associates with disease and beh
concern_text: Unclear how PpgAge could be interpreted in practical settings. If an individual has PpgAge gap of +2 years, what drives this? What is the practical implication for this specific individual?
author_response: Added interpretability analysis showing which PPG features drive age gap predictions.

paper_title: A wearable-based aging clock associates with disease and beh
concern_text: External validation in another dataset is strongly encouraged.
author_response: Discussed data availability limitations and added cross-validation robustness analysis.

paper_title: A wearable-based aging clock associates with disease and beh
concern_text: 'Wearable-based biomarker of aging' in the title may be an overstatement given current results. Please consider revising to more accurately reflect the study — central focus is chronological age prediction from PPG.
author_response: Revised title to be more precise.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: All survival analyses: using enrollment as start of follow-up is inappropriate. Time scale should be age, not calendar time. This is particularly important for Kaplan-Meier curves — age is not accommodated. Including age as covariate is typically not sufficient.
author_response: Re-ran all survival analyses with age as time scale.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: When looking at individual cancer entities, multiple testing adjustment should be considered. Renal pelvis cancer and leukemia will not be significant after correction.
author_response: Added Bonferroni correction and FDR-adjusted p-values.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: Cannot use future information on diabetes status to stratify at baseline in KM curves. Only baseline diabetes status is valid. In Cox model, diabetes could be a time-varying exposure.
author_response: Restricted to baseline diabetes status for KM. Added time-varying diabetes in Cox models.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: BMI-adjusted and unadjusted analyses done in different individuals (94,782 vs 20,938). Differences in effect sizes could be due to population differences, not BMI adjustment.
author_response: Re-ran both analyses in same population.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: Major concern about novelty — the metabolic syndrome is a well-known syndrome of insulin resistance with known cancer risk, easy to define clinically. Nowhere in the article do authors discuss the metabolic syndrome. Background literature linking metabolic syndrome to cancer is missing.
author_response: Added comprehensive metabolic syndrome comparison and discussion.

paper_title: Machine learning-predicted insulin resistance is a risk fact
concern_text: All lung cancer findings need to be adjusted or stratified by smoking status initially. Otherwise extremely difficult to interpret.
author_response: Added smoking-stratified analyses for all lung cancer associations.

paper_title: Machine learning center-specific models show improved IVF li
concern_text: Make new figure with real calibration plots for both models using 4-5 bins per clinic and overall. Include data distribution (TRIPOD example). Showing calibration plots is necessary to claim TRIPOD-AI adherence.
author_response: Added bin-based calibration plots with data distribution for all clinics.

paper_title: Machine learning center-specific models show improved IVF li
concern_text: Reported AUC improvements over age-only control seem very high (41%). Does age-only control have AUC <0.5? Results should be reported per clinic with 95% CI and paired DeLong test.
author_response: Added per-clinic AUC with CI and DeLong tests. Clarified age-only baseline.

paper_title: Machine learning center-specific models show improved IVF li
concern_text: Use TRIPOD+AI terminology ('internal validation data' not 'de novo model validation test set'). Missing descriptive table with differences between clinics. Need limitations section.
author_response: Adopted TRIPOD+AI terminology and added clinic comparison table and limitations.

paper_title: Machine learning center-specific models show improved IVF li
concern_text: Discussion gets too commercial ('Like many innovative products...', 'MLCS-based counseling reports...'). The commercial side should be toned down.
author_response: Removed commercial language.

paper_title: Machine learning center-specific models show improved IVF li
concern_text: Only aggregated data presented without individual center data. Either provide per-center data including number of patients, or change manuscript scope.
author_response: Added per-center performance tables and patient counts.

paper_title: Deep learning model for personalized prediction of positive
concern_text: Why focus only on MRSA when the clinical problem is more often 'should I give antibiotics for possible severe infection (sepsis)?' rather than specifically for MRSA? The narrow focus limits clinical utility.
author_response: Discussed MRSA as proof-of-concept with clearer outcome definition than sepsis. Future work will expand to broader infection prediction.

paper_title: Deep learning model for personalized prediction of positive
concern_text: Table 4 suggests benefits vs clinical judgment, but how was 'clinical judgment' determined? Was it based on antibiotic usage? How did authors check if antibiotic was given for MRSA vs something else? Should compare AUROC of DL model vs clinical judgment directly.
author_response: Clarified clinical judgment proxy and added direct AUROC comparison.

paper_title: Deep learning model for personalized prediction of positive
concern_text: Authors acknowledge using antibiotic prescribing as proxy for clinical judgment is a weakness. MRSA-specific antibiotics not exclusively used for MRSA (daptomycin/linezolid also target VRE).
author_response: Discussed limitations of antibiotic proxy and added sensitivity analysis.

paper_title: A highly accurate risk factor-based XGBoost multiethnic mode
concern_text: Hard to understand what model is predicting. Age not associated with skin cancer risk (line 181) but later stated as most important predictor (line 246). What are these conflicting results? Classification into ancestries also problematic — 'Hispanic' is not an ancestry, it is an ethnicity.
author_response: Clarified prediction target and ancestry vs ethnicity distinction. Resolved age contradiction.

paper_title: A highly accurate risk factor-based XGBoost multiethnic mode
concern_text: Given age was single most important predictor, how does an age-only model fare? PPV still substantially lower for non-Europeans — would worse performance be due to sample size or genuine differences?
author_response: Added age-only baseline comparison and sample-size sensitivity analysis for non-European groups.

paper_title: A highly accurate risk factor-based XGBoost multiethnic mode
concern_text: How were people classified into ancestries — self-report or PCA? How was Admixed group defined? Native American ancestry not included. Self-reported race vs genotype PCA — do they overlap?
author_response: Added PCA-based ancestry comparison alongside self-report.

paper_title: A highly accurate risk factor-based XGBoost multiethnic mode
concern_text: Only participants with complete data used (no NA values). How many participants remained after this exclusion?
author_response: Reported sample reduction and added sensitivity analysis with imputed data.

paper_title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and pro
concern_text: Metabolites could be triggered by other diseases — GSH:GSSG imbalance associated with lung cancers, HIV, immune dysfunction. Neopterin elevated in measles, influenza. How specific are the suggested biomarkers for gastric cancer?
author_response: Added disease-specificity analysis and multi-disease comparison.

paper_title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and pro
concern_text: Prognostic model with 28 variables but only 34 deceased cases — heavily biased toward survival. Should adopt orthogonal modeling or one-class approach, or prove model is unbiased.
author_response: Added class-weight adjustment and one-vs-rest validation.

paper_title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and pro
concern_text: Metabolites could be affected by diet habit, aging, or other diseases. Missing from cohort information: possible other underlying diseases and nutritional habits. ML model's false positive discovery rate should be addressed.
author_response: Added diet and comorbidity data as confounders.

paper_title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and pro
concern_text: 258 vs 147 metabolites discrepancy. LOQ, LODs, ion transitions for MRM, main adduct ions and retention time should be provided. How is relative abundance calculated — quantitative or normalized peak area?
author_response: Clarified metabolite filtering pipeline and added analytical validation parameters.

paper_title: Prediction of plasma ctDNA fraction and prognostic implicati
concern_text: Most samples were already analyzed in previous publications from same group. Prognostic association of ctDNA is not novel — the strength is the AI prediction tool. Title and narrative should center on the predictive tool, not the prognostic role of ctDNA.
author_response: Restructured narrative to emphasize the prediction tool as main contribution.

paper_title: Prediction of plasma ctDNA fraction and prognostic implicati
concern_text: Patients exposed to taxanes had increased cfDNA and ctDNA fraction. How does the prediction model account for ctDNA variance due to different therapies if these variables were not incorporated?
author_response: Added therapy-stratified analysis and discussed model behavior across treatment lines.

paper_title: Prediction of plasma ctDNA fraction and prognostic implicati
concern_text: cfDNA concentration seems to be the highest predictor of ctDNA fraction and is inter-correlated with LDH/ALP. But authors don't explore cfDNA concentration's prognostic role or compare it to ctDNA.
author_response: Added cfDNA concentration as standalone prognostic factor comparison.

paper_title: Predicting response to enzalutamide and abiraterone in metas
concern_text: Most patients (even in academic centers) do not undergo WGS/WTS. It would be of great practical relevance to study model performance with targeted panel sequencing data as input, ideally in a separate cohort.
author_response: Discussed panel sequencing as future work and showed which features are capturable by commercial panels.

paper_title: Predicting response to enzalutamide and abiraterone in metas
concern_text: Not clear how treatment response to ARSI can be differentiated from overall prognosis. Is the model predicting aggressive disease rather than features specific to ARSI response?
author_response: Added treatment-specific interaction analysis and discussed prognostic vs predictive biomarkers.

paper_title: Predicting response to enzalutamide and abiraterone in metas
concern_text: Figure legends too small to be readable. Figure resolution poor. Distribution of variables not shown. No exploration of how validation cohort differs from training cohort.
author_response: Improved all figures and added cohort comparison.

paper_title: Predicting response to enzalutamide and abiraterone in metas
concern_text: Choice of sparse PCA as feature reduction is well-established but not without difficulties. Covariance of features, captured variance for number of components should be shown. Why logistic regression and not other methods?
author_response: Added PCA variance explained plots and comparison with other classifiers.

paper_title: Personalized risk stratification in colorectal cancer via PI
concern_text: Outcome used in benchmarking is 3-year recurrence, but several benchmark methods were developed for 5-year OS/RFS. Should tabulate timepoint and outcome metric for each benchmark method — risk of comparing apples and pears.
author_response: Added table comparing timepoints and outcome metrics across all benchmarked methods.

paper_title: Personalized risk stratification in colorectal cancer via PI
concern_text: Can performance be benchmarked to mIHC scores such as ImmunoScore and SIA? Should include iCMS system and CRPS system (Nunes 2024) for comparison.
author_response: Added ImmunoScore and CRPS comparison.
